investigations.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator
fuels: C2H4/N2 on 25 mm and 50 mm porous burners

conditions.note: Habitat atmospheres considered by NASA, as stated in the PSI objectives.

investigations.summary: A gas burner that emulates how solid materials burn in a still atmosphere, tested in the atmospheres planned for spacecraft and bases.

findings.text: Quasi-steady burning of condensed-phase materials such as PMMA and Nylon was observed in microgravity with NO air flow, notably in the oxygen-enriched atmospheres being considered for future spacecraft; at 21% O2 such flames self-extinguished in a short time.
Cutting ventilation is an established step to put out spacecraft fires; these results suggest it may not be enough in oxygen-rich atmospheres.
The authors suggest NASA may want to make more use of its alternative flammability Test 2 (cone calorimeter), which can measure material properties matching the microgravity flames seen with BRE.

investigations.spaceApplication: Material selection and fire-response protocols for lunar habitat atmospheres.

investigations.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids
fuels: PMMA (flat samples and 1 cm and 2 cm spheres)

conditions.note: 41 samples and 89 test points. The O2 range is not given in the fact sheet.

investigations.summary: Burns solid samples in a controlled-flow duct inside the Microgravity Science Glovebox and extinguishes the flame by ramping up a nitrogen flow.

findings.text: Recent BASS results indicate that NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is NOT conservative: materials can burn at lower oxygen levels in microgravity than on Earth.
Local application of suppressant is not adequate for extinguishment: the local jet entrains air and sustains the flame even when the ambient airflow is turned off.
Hypothesis: with adequate ventilation, materials in microgravity burn as well if not better than in normal gravity under otherwise identical conditions.

investigations.spaceApplication: NASA's spacecraft materials selection relies on a 1-g standard test (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1) that ignores low-gravity effects.
investigations.earthApplication: Validates combustion models used for terrestrial problems.

investigations.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment

conditions.note: O2 and pressure are MEASURED ranges across the 274 tests in the PSI-69 table (pressures cluster at 0.70, 1.0, 2.0, 2.7 and 3.05 atm). The fact sheet planned O2 0.10–0.50 and 0.5–1.0 atm. The main diluent is N2, with a few tests using He.

investigations.summary: Burns fuel droplets in mixtures of oxygen and diluents to map flammability limits and the effectiveness of inert suppressants (CO2, He).

findings.text: The flammability limit is lower in reduced gravity; terrestrial standards for inert-gas suppressants do not offer the same margin of safety in low gravity.
Demonstrated radiative and diffusive extinction, combustion instabilities, lower flammability limits and explained the cool-flame phenomenon after visible flame extinction.
Low pressures are tested because one extinguishing strategy is to isolate the habitat and vent the cabin to space.

Of the 274 recorded tests, 186 ended in extinction, 61 in disruption and 27 in completion. At lunar-habitat-like conditions (0.6–0.8 atm and O2 ≥ 26.5%) there are 17 tests and none ended in extinction (15 disruption, 2 completion).

investigations.spaceApplication: Provides the most conservative estimate of the limiting oxygen index (LOI) for steady combustion.
investigations.earthApplication: Heptane and methanol models are building blocks for practical fuels such as diesel and jet fuel.

investigations.title: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
fuels: dibutyl phthalate on a porous wick

conditions.note: 30 samples (6 per material) at different airflow rates, heating temperatures and smoke aging times. ISS Expedition 15.

investigations.summary: Measures the size and distribution of smoke particles from spacecraft materials and evaluates ionization (Shuttle) and photoelectric (ISS) smoke detectors.

findings.text: All samples produced significant numbers of sub-micron particles, better detected by an ionization detector; a light-scattering detector would perform very well for most cases.
Arithmetic mean diameters are 100 to 200 nm; for silicone rubber (227 nm) almost half the particle mass is in particles larger than 1000 nm.
The detection target is the early phase (pre-fire heating products), not soot; detectors that measure a wider size spectrum may be more reliable.

investigations.spaceApplication: A low-gravity smoke baseline against which future detection technology can be evaluated.
investigations.earthApplication: Smoke detectors useful in submarines and underwater laboratories.

incidents.name: Apollo 1
incidents.text: A flash fire swept the Command Module during a pre-launch test in a 100% oxygen cabin. Grissom, White and Chaffee died. The three-piece hatch took about 90 seconds to open.
incidents.lesson: A unified hatch that opens in 3 seconds, tightly restricted combustible materials and fire-resistant spacesuits.

incidents.name: Apollo 13
incidents.text: Oxygen tank no. 2 exploded en route to the Moon after its heaters overheated and degraded the Teflon insulation; heater voltage had been raised from 28 to 65 V DC without upgrading the thermostats.
incidents.lesson: Oxygen system redesign: a third tank, upgraded thermostats, no stirring fans and stainless-steel-sheathed wiring.

incidents.name: Mir
incidents.text: On 24 February a solid-fuel oxygen generator canister caught fire in the Kvant-1 module. The flame burned for several minutes and the crew fought it with foam extinguishers.
incidents.lesson: Changes to canister preparation and emergency training; the ISS uses dissimilar, redundant oxygen generation.

incidents.name: Artemis II
incidents.text: A smoke alarm sounded about 80,000 miles from Earth, as recounted by the commander in the challenge statement.
incidents.lesson: A reminder of why fast detection and response matter far from home.

spinoffs.name: Firefighter air tank
spinoffs.text: A 20 lb backpack with a 30-minute air supply at 4,500 psi (13 lb lighter than conventional tanks), with an aluminum liner wrapped in glass fibers.

spinoffs.name: Project FIRES: protective clothing
spinoffs.text: Firefighter protective gear using fire-resistant fabrics derived from spacesuit materials, field-tested in 14 municipal fire departments.

spinoffs.name: Brunswick Incipient Fire Detector
spinoffs.text: A Space Shuttle detector that tells combustion particles from dust (fewer false alarms) and senses fire before flame and smoke; sensors can be networked for mines.
